F1 in SA

By: Floris Kotze | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Formula 1, could make a return to the African continent after a very long 30 year hiatus! What does this mean for SA? What can we expect? One thing is clear, there are a lot of excited fans!

Unique Selling Point:
A feel-good story about the potential return of F1 to South Africa. We visit a few small businesses that might benefit from this! We speak to people on the ground and find out exactly how passionate these fans are, even if they won't be able to go to the race its-self.



Summary:
We speak to Peter Windsor, an F1 journalist and former Williams team member. He has been involved with Formula 1 since the early 70's and has been to Kyalami, racing with the Williams team.
We will try and do links at Kyalami, however, they won't be able to comment before the news breaks.
I will speak to Sasha Marteningo (after clearance), he has been at the forefront of the media frenzy, since it broke late May 2022. He will bring us up to speed with the latest news.
We aim to speak to Dept of Sports and Culture - initial talks are positive. We will also approach a prominent YouTuber from Joburg, excited and beyond himself, we will try and carry this energy over to viewers.


Further information:
Formula 1 (F1) may be making its way to South Africa for the first time in 30 years. It was reported in late May that F1 was working towards a deal to see South Africa rejoin the international race calendar in time for 2023.

Insert Treatment - It will be a high-impact, lots of energy insert. We will have photos to explain the drama and excitement F1 brings to a country. Unfortunately, we are not allowed to use any F1 footage.
We aim to film some Voxies from a few South Africans, to hear their input.

Goals - 1. To share a good news story, and generate excitement. 2. Experts will explain the benefits to South Africa, 3. We will also touch on the prices for the tickets.

Confirmed interviews: Peter Windsor, Sasha Martinengo

Unconfirmed interviews: The Minister of Sport, Arts, and Culture (DSAC), Nathi Mthethwa, Jody Scheckter , Kyalami Circuit.

Exciting for all of us - Not only for F1 Fans. We aim to convince the average, non-motorsport South African fan, of the importance of F1 in SA, and in doing that, we generate more excitement for all of us!

Script:


Jimmy Clark Opening
Engine Noises
Montage
20 Starters in the South African Grand Prix at East London….
VO:
South Africa has a rich history in motorsports…
Gunter BRM overtakes the South African entered Alfa Special…
VO:
East London, hosted the South African Grand Prix, from the early 1930’s to the mid 60’s, here at the Prince George Circuit…
Jim Clark the first driver ever to win 7 world championship events in a season.
And look at that…. It is all happening here at Kyalami…
VO:
The event moved to the historical Kyalami Circuit in the late 60’s, with the last South African Formula One race held here, in 1993. History might soon repeat itself…
Montage:
Almost 30 years after the Last Formula One Grand Prix in South Africa - glimpses of Formula 1 returning to the Nation….
There are heavy rumours that suggest the South African Grand Prix will be returning to no better place than Kyalami…
Fade to black
LINK
This is Hammanskraal, about an hour's drive, North of Pretoria. Right here there is a passion for speed that would rival the fans at any Formula one track around the world.
Derek:
Dumelang?
Hendrick:
Morning morning morning…
Henrick: Ja it’s Hendrick…
Derek:
Henrick? How are you doing? I am Derek…


Hendrick:
Me I am Hendrick the Artist…
VO: Hendrik Chebanga discovered he had a talent for art 14 years ago.
When Hendrick first heard about the possibility of Formula 1 returning to South Africa,
he jumped at the opportunity to create something special, to demonstrate his love for F1.
Derek:
Wow Hendrick…
So you are a Hamilton fan?
Hendrick: Yes, yes, I love him…
Derek: And where did your love for racing Formula one start, Hendrick?
Hendrick:
Since I was a small boy,
We used to make the wire cars and do some races.
Derek:
Are you keen for a Formula 1 race in South Africa?
Yes! I heard that it is coming to South Africa,
It is going to be amazing, just to touch it, the real one!
Derek: You would just love that?
Hendrick: I would love that!

VO: Hendrick is certainly not the only person wishing that Formula 1 would make a return to South Africa…
VO:
Sir Lewis Hamilton, a current F1 driver and 7-time driver’s world champion, has voiced his opinion on racing in South Africa many times….
PW
Lewis loves South Africa and feels very emotional about South Africa. I think it will be a great shame and remiss of Formula 1 if we don’t go back to South Africa during Lewis’ active time in Formula 1.

VO:
Peter Windsor is a Formula 1 journalist and former Formula 1 team manager. He started reporting on F1 back in the 70’s. He shares his memories of his very first visit to Johannesburg.
PW:
We walked out of the receptionist area, and there were Mario Andretti, Clay Regazzoni, Peter Sheddy, Jacky Stewart, Francois Cevert all sitting around by the pool. And they were all incredibly nice, you know, I can’t even imagine anything like that happening today.
Most of my memory was the original Kyalami, compared to anything else on the calendar, it was unique
It had it’s own atmosphere, it had it’s own characteristic. I would love to see South Africa back on the calendar. And I think I speak for many people in Formula 1 when I say that.
Link:
Lauda, Mansell, Senna, Schumacker and our very own Jody Scheckter, so many world champions and famous names have raced here at Kyalami, but that was decades ago, so now imagine, Verstappen, Le Clerc, Hamilton, you name it, right here on the starting grid. I think it would be a tad noisier.
Montage F1
Montage of Talks collapse
It’s not great news at this moment because the prospect of South Africa hosting a Formula 1 race next year is gone…
South Africa have become more uncertain…
Kyalami won’t be happening next year…
There won’t be a race for 2023…
SM
The facility is there, the infrastructure of South Africa is ready for it, despite what anybody else can say… We can host this thing, and the people are extremely excited!
VO:
Sasha Martinengo, a veteran in the broadcast industry, would love nothing more than to see the prancing horse take to Kyalami.
SM
If we got 60 000 people that can fit into Kyalami, I can guarantee you at least 25 000 of those, or even more, would come from probably Europe, United States, even Australia and they are not only going to spend 3 days here, they are going to spend 2 weeks here. That money is going to filter into our economy, putting us back on the map in a much more positive light.
LINK
But getting onto that map doesn't come cheap so is it worth the cash we'd have to cough up


VO:
The fee South Africa has to pay in order to host the race is unknown. According to reports, other countries have paid Formula One anything between $15 Million to $50 Million….
Toby Venter
It is expensive, and it’s got to be funded correctly to make sure it continues...
VO:
Toby Venter is the owner of Kyalami Grand Prix circuit. A racer by heart, he's been hard at work to try and bring Formula one back to South Africa. He took me for a few laps around Kyalami….
In Car
Derek: Tricky one, hey Toby?
TV:
A Grand Prix would be great for the country. The business model is difficult and a lot of the governments support the Grand Prix with funding because it benefits the country as a whole. In this case we haven't been able to secure government funding, government has got other difficulties and priorities, but we hope that we can put a Consortium of promoters and investors together to ensure that we do actually get a Grand Prix in the future. But we need an international investor and international sponsor to get them the benefit.
MT:
For anything to happen of this magnitude the cash doesn't come overnight people need to budget .
VO:
Miguel Tiago is a SuperSport commentator and represents the F.I.A. in Africa. The F.I.A. is the governing body for multiple motorsports events, including Formula One.

MT:
The promoters is something that the FIA don’t specifically like to get involved with, because they have to go hand in hand with the government. So it’s a question of the government and the promoters being on the same frequency. Because the rest has happened already. The rest is in place. We’re looking specifically for a promoter, for someone who will come in for 2 or 3 years so that F1 can stay in Africa for as long as possible.
Derek:
How motivated are you to see a F1 Grand Prix right here?
Toby:
I'm very motivated and I do believe we will see a Grand Prix one-day…
Derek:
People are hoping for 2024?


Toby:
I'm also hoping for 2024 as we speak, there are talks taking place in London and hopefully in the next couple of weeks we will hear good news…
VO:
We asked a few South Africans for their thoughts on Formula One in Africa.

UPSOUNDS:
1: Pushing it out to 24 allows South Africa as a country and as a community to truly galvanise, and promote the race and put on something that's gonna be absolutely world-class and spectacular in the way that we know how.

2: It’s going to have a socio-economic impact obviously, maybe good and bad, you know, do we have the infrastructure, should we be spending the money on something else, should we be focusing on something else? But then you gotta think of that flip side of the, you know how many people it's going to attract our country and how many jobs it's going to create…

3: It will basically be the best advertisement to the largest audience we can ever imagine,our country reaching, I just don't see how that could be a bad thing.

4: I'm really excited for F1 to potentially come to Africa, South Africa. For Africa as a whole, it is going to be quite exciting once we can get the government to assist, that way you'll be able to get a few low income earners, who really love the sport, to come and witness this.
LINK:
Looks like we won't be hearing ‘lights out and away we go’ in South Africa next year but Hendrick and so many other passionate fans must be hoping even praying, that we will hear the roar of Formula 1 engines in 2024 !
Outro
